$comment: Tests written ahead of their feature: each must FAIL until the feature is in, then come off this list. See tests/README.md (red first). Only new tests belong here; the floor guard refuses an existing test listed as pending.

pending.test: river: the outer ring of a 13x13 board is its 48 edge points, clockwise, each once
river: a creature can come up in front of every edge point on all four sides: 52 spots on 13x13
river: a creature reaches three outer-ring points, the one it faces and its two neighbours along the ring
river: the D6 is rolled every 5 turns, never on turn 0, and only a 5 or 6 brings a creature
river: after a 5 or 6 the crab comes two times in three, the spirit one time in three
river: its timer is 3 rounds, counted in turns for the table, and shows the rounds left
river: a second creature only comes up where its reach doesn't touch the first one's
river: the crab pinches one stone in reach at random, the spirit steals every one of them
river creatures: no roll until the Night Market is open for the whole table
river creatures: a D6 every 5 turns; a 1 to 4 brings nothing, with the same odds next time
river creatures: on a 5 or 6 a crab or a spirit climbs onto the pier, facing an edge point, with three points in reach and a 3-round timer
river creatures: the crab waits out its timer, then pinches one stone in reach, picked at random
river creatures: the spirit waits out its timer, then steals every stone in its reach
river creatures: stones outside the reach are left alone, and with none in reach it leaves empty-handed
river creatures: a warded, fogged or misted stone, or driftwood, is safe from both
river creatures: each stone taken pays its owner 3 fireflies, and nobody gets a prisoner
river creatures: at most one crab and one spirit at a time; a roll for one already out brings nothing
river creatures: their news is added to the turn's event, not put in its place
river creatures: a game that ends while they are out sends them back into the water
river creatures: a bot's view shows each one that is out, with its reach and the turns it has left
river creatures: they and their timers survive a snapshot restore
bait: always on sale at the Night Market, beside the six drawn stalls
bait: fed to a creature through a point in its reach, it goes back into the water and takes nothing
bait: using it doesn't use up the turn
bait: refused and kept with no creature out, or on a point outside every reach
bait: with both out, it drives off only the one whose reach holds the point
bait: anyone may feed a creature, whoever's stones are in its reach
bait: the Bait can be bought from the start of the market, as any stall
bots: a bot holding a Bait feeds a creature that will take its stone before its next turn
bots: a bot buys a Bait when a creature has its stone in reach, and not otherwise
bots: a point in a creature's reach ranks below the same point with none out
river creatures: they stand on the board's wooden frame in front of the edge point they face, on all four sides, off the grid
river creatures: crab and spirit climb out, idle, take, go back into the water; or, fed a Bait, eat it and go
river creatures: every phase of both is drawn in the palette, they move while they idle, and their reach is ringed while they wait
river creatures: the timer over their head shows the rounds left
river creatures: the crab's stone and every stone the spirit steals leave in its hands, not as a capture
river creatures over the wire: every client sees a crab or a spirit come up on a 5 or 6, where it stands, its reach and its timer
river creatures over the wire: a Bait bought and fed by the player on turn sends it back into the water
river creatures over the wire: when its timer runs out it has gone back into the water, with stones from its reach only
game: How to play tells of the river crab and the river spirit, their D6 and the Bait
game: the Bait stall is in the market every night
game: a river creature climbs onto the pier on the page, its reach ringed and its timer shown, in palette colours
game: when its timer runs out the river creature goes back into the water on the page
